What is Quarto?

Quarto is an open-source scientific and technical publishing system built to help create high-quality reproducible documents, presentations, websites and more.



Does it sound familiar?






Yes! Quarto is the next generation of R Markdown.

title: Creating simple websites with Quarto + GitHub Pages
text:
Building websites with Quarto

There are lots of cool things you can do with Quarto, like making:

📃 reports

section: What do all the different files do?
text:
What do all the different files do?











The index.qmd file is essential. When a qmd file is named as index, it will automatically be used as the home page.
The index.qmd file must be named exactly as it is: index.qmd.
The index.qmd file must be placed in the root folder next to the _quarto.yml.

What do all the different files do?











The about.qmd is the the ‘About’ page in your website.
It’s a model for how we can add extra pages (we’ll try this later!)

text:
How does it all come together?
my-website/
├── _quarto.yml       ← 🔧 Configuration file
├── styles.css        ← 🎨 Custom styling (optional)
├── index.qmd         ← 🏠 Home page
├── about.qmd         ← 📄 Additional page
└── _site/            ← 🌐 Rendered website output (auto-generated)
The goal today is to make sure that everyone will have a working website published via Github Pages to take home!

First, we’ll open up RStudio & create a new project of the type ‘Quarto website’

title: Creating simple websites with Quarto + GitHub Pages
text:
Hosting our website
But how can we share this website with others?

This is where GitHub pages comes in!


It’s a free way to host our website from a GitHub repository.



We can set up git for our project using the usethis package

title: Creating simple websites with Quarto + GitHub Pages
text:
Setting up git
Git is probably already installed on your computer, but if not you should install it now.
Then, we can use usethis to initialise git locally:

# if you haven't installed 'usethis' before
install.packages("usethis")

# setup git repo
usethis::use_git()

And put this local git repository onto GitHub:

usethis::use_github()

If you’ve never used git before, you might need to provide it with your details:

# obviously change these to your own!!
usethis::use_git_config(
  user.name = "kzeglinski",
  user.email = "kathleen.j.zeglinski@gmail.com')

text:

title: Creating simple websites with Quarto + GitHub Pages
text:
Publishing the website
The final step we need to do is publish the website to GitHub pages

To do this, go to the ‘terminal’ tab next to the R console:

title: Creating simple websites with Quarto + GitHub Pages
text:
Publishing the website
And run the following command:
quarto publish gh-pages


You’ll need to do this every time you want to update your website



Hopefully you’ll see your new website pop up now!

text:
Now for the fun part!
Once the website is setup, you can start customising it! Luckily, Quarto makes it easy for us to do this with the visual editor:


You can easily add images or tables, and style your text

title: Creating simple websites with Quarto + GitHub Pages
text:
Now for the fun part!
You can preview your changes with the ‘render’ button, and publish them to the web with the same quarto publish gh-pages command from earlier, and they should appear on your website

But what if we want to add extra pages to our website?

title: Creating simple websites with Quarto + GitHub Pages
text:
Adding extra pages
There are two things we need to do to add an extra page:



Create a new .qmd file for that page

title: Creating simple websites with Quarto + GitHub Pages
text:
Adding extra pages

Add this new page to the _quarto.yml


You can add as many pages as you want!

title: Creating simple websites with Quarto + GitHub Pages
text:
Changing the theme
While we’ve got the _quarto.yml open, it’s a good oppotunity to change the theme! Quarto contains a range of built in themes that we can use by simply editing the ‘theme’ portion of the YAML file:
format:
  html:
    theme: litera
    css: styles.css
    toc: true

title: Creating simple websites with Quarto + GitHub Pages
text:
Summary
To create a new Quarto website:

Use the ‘new project’ button in RStudio
Set up git and GitHub:

usethis::use_git()
usethis::use_github()
Alternatively, you can use GitHub Desktop or the git command line.

Publish website to GitHub pages

quarto publish gh-pages

title: Creating simple websites with Quarto + GitHub Pages
text:
Summary
To update a Quarto website:

Make your desired changes, use the visual editor to help you!
Use the render button to check everything looks ok
Publish to GitHub pages

quarto publish gh-pages
